lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Pilgrimage and Hajj
lesson.summary: Learn what pilgrimage means, follow the steps of Hajj, and see why journeys matter to many faiths.
learning_objectives: Describe the main steps of Hajj
Compare Hajj with another pilgrimage with respect

standards.text: Pilgrimage in Islam and other faiths: Hajj, Jerusalem and Karbala

success_criteria: I can say what a pilgrimage is
I can put the steps of Hajj in order
I can talk about other pilgrimages with respect
lesson.real_life: British Pakistani Hajj groups, Hajj flights from Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad, Hajj stories from elders, and talks at the local mosque.

blocks.markdown: A **pilgrimage** is a journey to a holy place for faith.
blocks.say: A pilgrimage is a journey to a holy place. People make it because of their faith.

blocks.title: Faiza hears a Hajj story
blocks.transcript: Faiza's grandfather tells her about his Hajj. First he wore the simple clothes of ihram. He walked around the Ka'bah seven times. He drank Zamzam water and walked between Safa and Marwah. On the ninth day he prayed on the plain of Arafat. At night he rested at Muzdalifah. Then came Eid al-Adha, with prayer and sharing. Faiza learns that in Hajj, everyone stands as equals.
blocks.caption: Faiza hears her grandfather's Hajj story and follows the steps in order from ihram to Eid.

blocks.markdown: **Ihram** is the simple clothing and sacred state of a pilgrim.
blocks.say: Pilgrims enter a state called ihram. Men wear two plain white cloths.

blocks.markdown: Rich and poor stand side by side.
blocks.say: Women wear simple, modest clothes. Everyone looks alike, so all are equal before Allah.

blocks.markdown: **Tawaf** is walking around the Ka'bah seven times.
blocks.say: Then they walk around the Ka'bah seven times. This is called tawaf.

blocks.markdown: The Day of Arafat is the heart of Hajj.
